narrative.overview:
The portal is a calm, light working space: frosted frames float over a pale wash that deepens from white at the top left to soft violet at the bottom right. Every piece of content sits on a solid white panel set inside a translucent frame, so the glass gives the page depth while the text always reads on white. Ink, a near-black violet, is the only strong neutral and it carries meaning: where you are, and the one thing to do next. Colour beyond that belongs to subjects, and on a home surface only one subject is allowed to be loud.

The world was built for the admin and tutor portals and now carries the student portal on the same shell, kit and tokens. Density is moderate: compact rows (about 60px) with one action each, a 20px gutter between frames, and type that is bold rather than large. Hierarchy comes from weight, one saturated fill and placement, not from decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Translucent glass frames with a 6px inset around solid white panels.
Fixed diagonal wash behind everything, holding still while the window scrolls.
Figtree throughout, extrabold (800) for titles and numbers, no separate display face.
Ink fills reserved for the current location, the primary action, today and counts.
Subject tones as pale fills, with one saturated subject on a home surface.
Status colours (good, warn, bad, info) kept to tinted icon tiles and due chips.

rules.name: The Subjects Own Colour Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour on a page belongs to subjects; chrome, headers and panels stay ink, white and glass.

rules.name: The One Saturated Subject Rule
rules.body: On a home surface every subject is its pale fill except one, the subject on now or next, which takes its solid fill with white text; a live lesson chip in the week list is the only other solid.

rules.name: The Ink Means Here Rule
rules.body: An ink fill says "you are here" or "do this": the active nav item, the selected segment, today, the primary button, a count. A feature link that is neither (the student's Taiyo Blitz entry) is white, not ink.

rules.name: The Weight Not Size Rule
rules.body: Raise importance with weight (800) before size; the page title is only 22px.

rules.name: The Functional Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is for nav group headings (0.1em), weekday abbreviations in a date column (0.06em) and the TUITION wordmark only; nothing sits above a title as a kicker.

rules.name: The Text On White Rule
rules.body: Glass carries titles and controls; content always sits on a solid white panel, so readability never depends on what is behind the frame.

dos: Do put every surface on the shared glass shell and kit (PageHeader, GlassPanel, TodoPanel, buttonVariants) so a feature looks the same in each role.
Do set content on the white panel inside a frame, never directly on glass.
Do give exactly one subject its solid fill on a home surface, the subject on now or next, and keep the rest pale.
Do make the featured card's next lesson its largest text (18px extrabold).
Do reserve ink fills for the active nav item, the selected segment, today, the primary action and counts.
Do turn finished items neutral (neutral fill, muted text) instead of lowering their opacity.
Do use ink-soft, not muted, for secondary text that sits on the wash or on glass.
Do keep hover motion to a 2-3px rise and a deeper shadow over 150-200ms.
donts: Don't open a page with a saturated greeting hero; the page header is a glass strip with the title, the date and term, and at most one ink action.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a title; the title stands alone.
Don't paint chrome, headers or whole panels in a subject or brand colour.
Don't give more than one subject card its saturated fill at once.
Don't add progress rings, confetti or celebration graphics to a portal home.
Don't append a status pill to every To do row or subject card; a row's state lives in its icon tile tone and its single action.
Don't use a subject tone to mean a status, or a status colour to mean a subject.
Don't substitute framework defaults for the radius and shadow values above.
